title: Compute efficiency: binary keeps only 2% of the multipliers busy

body:
With NX8's 8-bit static formats, the tensor that loses most even in its best format is layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256: 32.1 dB SQNR (signal-to-quantization-noise ratio; higher is better) in fp8_e2m5, measured on that tensor alone by the format search. Measured on 7 models with a format search (of 513 surveyed).

Model outputs keep a median 26.9 dB SQNR against full precision, the worst 12.7 dB (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae). 5 of 7 models with a prediction metric (top-1, perplexity or agreement) lose some of it; the most: facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (token agreement 100% → 64%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's), stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (token agreement 100% → 68%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's) and openai-community/gpt2 (perplexity 47 → 52.5, higher is worse).

The tensors that lose most in their best format (their own error): layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 32.1 dB), add output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 34.0 dB), layernorm bias in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 34.2 dB), mul output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 34.5 dB), layernorm bias in openai-community/gpt2 (fp8_e3m4, 34.5 dB), linear bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 34.7 dB), layernorm output in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 35.5 dB), linear output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 35.5 dB), linear output in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e3m4, 35.8 dB) and groupnorm bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 35.8 dB).

Separately, the error accumulated along the data path (every tensor before a node quantized too): mul outputs end furthest from full precision, facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 keeping only -0.8 dB there. The outputs furthest from full precision in each model's best format set: mul in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, -0.8 dB), softmax in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e1m6, 1.9 dB), bmm in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e2m5, 4.0 dB), linear in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e2m5, 4.4 dB), linear in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 7.6 dB), attention in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 9.2 dB), linear in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 9.2 dB), silu in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 10.5 dB), attention in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 11.1 dB) and add in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 11.3 dB).

Formats chosen (E = exponent bits, M = mantissa bits, u = unsigned): fp8_e2m5 3996 (74%), fp8_e1m6 940 (17%), fp8_e3m4 474 (8.76%); 0% of tensors use an unsigned format.

A wider format or a per-row choice would recover most where a tensor's own error in its format, times its data, is largest: silu output in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e2m5, 42.4 dB), conv2d weight in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e2m5, 42.7 dB) and conv2d bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e2m5, 43.2 dB).

**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip).** The chip cannot read memory at an address computed at run time, so every lookup or choice by a run-time value (embedding) needs a workaround. It affects 29 operations in 1 model: 29 calls (1.15% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: embedding in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256. Cost today: 0 of 29 have a workaround (0 exact, 0 approximate), 0 failed and 29 wait for one; 18 workarounds proposed, 0 passing its check, 4 evaluated on a model; accuracy not measured yet; cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

title: Missing instructions: 29 operations in 1 model need workarounds

body:
A kernel reads a tensor in the arrangement its writer stored it in; when the reader needs another arrangement, the reading kernel has to rearrange the data itself. This happens to 481 of 678 tensors passed between kernels (71%) in 5 models: 315 for attention heads split or merged, 147 for other reshapes, 16 for pixels reordered and 3 for image patches.

The reading operations are 307 operations (307 calls, 12% of all calls; 75.5 G MACs, 13% of all MACs). The most common causes (writer → reader): linear → attention (attention heads split or merged) 207, linear → bmm (attention heads split or merged) 108 and linear → mul (other reshapes) 56; most in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (196), stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (128) and jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (88).

Cost today: extra cycles not measured yet (no reading kernel has run); 0 links fail.
title: Layout conversions: 481 of 678 tensors between kernels are rearranged

body:
Activations such as exp, GELU and reciprocal go through a 256-entry lookup table (LUT), which limits their precision: 712 operations in 5 models (712 calls, 28% of all calls), most often layernorm (208), silu (160) and attention (69). Their quantized accuracy: worst 1.9 dB SQNR over 712 measured operations.

Kernels per forward pass (host launches, one per planned kernel call): median 41, most 58 (facebook/DiT-XL-2-256, 58 planned groups), over 5 models.

FP32 headroom (how far the largest value is from FP32 overflow, in powers of ten) is least at 33.4 powers of ten for bmm in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (largest value 1.35e+05).

13 outputs in 1 model hold a value at the FP32 limit itself (mostly add (12) and select_where (1), e.g. an attention mask's fill value); they are counted apart from the headroom.

0 kernels use over 80% of the 1,024-word instruction memory (IMEM) bank, of 2 kernels measured.
title: Resource limits: 712 operations limited by the LUT and up to 58 kernel launches per pass

body:
The largest measured cost is accuracy from 8-bit quantization: model outputs keep a median 24.4 dB SQNR against full precision (worst 12.7 dB for stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae), and 5 of 7 models lose prediction quality — worst facebook/DiT-XL-2-256, whose token agreement drops from 100% to 59% — with layernorm biases the weakest single tensors (~34 dB even in their best formats).

Next, 31 operations in 3 models (30 embeddings needing run-time addressing, 1 aten::conv1d) have no workaround implemented, so they cannot run on the chip's direct path yet, though they hold almost no MACs and so far add no extra kernels.

Layout rearrangement is the most widespread overhead: 524 of 741 inter-kernel tensors (71%) must be rearranged by their reading kernel — 338 operations, 11% of calls and 3.41% of MACs, mostly for attention head splits/merges — with the cycle cost not yet measured.

Resource limits add further cost: 867 operations (29% of calls) route through the 256-entry LUT (quantized accuracy unmeasured), and a forward pass launches a median 13 kernels, up to 58 for facebook/DiT-XL-2-256.

Finally, error compounds along the data path (mul outputs in DiT-XL-2-256 sit at −3.8 dB), and MAC utilisation, cycles, and IMEM use are all still unmeasured because no kernel has been built or run.
